identity.note: Consolidated under the standing rule (see the collision-rule erratum, 2026-08-30), on a Fejona-class convergence (data/review-queue.json #268, the fullest evidence chain this sweep found): (1) name plus moniker exactly, "'Diamond Girl' Heidi Leick" on GDWA's own card of 18 January 2000 matching the ranked entity's own aka; (2) the ranked placings (1998 #136, 1999 #44) sit immediately before that card, an adjacent era; (3) GDWA's own home page links the IEWA by full name as a women's-division fed, matching the 1999 ranked entry's own IEWA tag — GDWA's own document naming the linked federation; (4) a workshop-held (not served) newsgroup posting corroborates both exact placings under a signature naming the same handler; (5) that handler is the same one GDWA's own site credits for building it. Five independent signals converging on one performer, short of an explicit document but well past presumption. Graded presumed rather than user-attested: no ruling has been quoted for this specific pair. This is a NAMESAKE case, not a portrayal, and that finding is untouched by this merge — the character is named for actress Hudson Leick (Callisto in Xena), not staged as her; the `portrays` edge to `hudson-leick` in data/external-figures.json stays exactly as filed. the-diamond-girl-heidi-leick-rspwf is retired; its RSPWF Top 200 bestowals repoint here. diamond-napw remains a separate, undisturbed distinct filing — an ordinary coincidence on the word "Diamond" and nothing more.

portrays.note: Named for the actress, and specifically for her real given name: Hudson Leick, Callisto in Xena: Warrior Princess, was born Heidi Hudson Leick. GDWA's character takes the true first name rather than the billed one. No GDWA document states the borrowing — the fed's own pages never mention the actress — so this is a reading of the name, not the fed's own claim, and it is a NAMESAKE and not a portrayal: GDWA barred real wrestlers and this is an original character of its own, not the actress staged as herself.
